dotnet linq2db - Linq To DB command-line utilities. Version: 6.4.0.0

Usage:
        dotnet linq2db [help]: print this help
        dotnet linq2db help <command>: print help on specific command
        dotnet linq2db <command> [<options>]: execute specific command

linq2db tool provides database model scaffolding (reverse engineering) of database into Linq To DB (https://linq2db.github.io/) database model classes.

Supported commands:
        dotnet linq2db config-init <options> : create or update a query/MCP configuration profile; generated profiles intentionally include maxRows, output, and enableExecute for manual editing
        dotnet linq2db credentials <set|list|remove|clear> [options] : manage encrypted linq2db credential profiles in the current user's system credential store
        dotnet linq2db execute <options> : execute write-capable SQL statement using a trusted profile with enableExecute set
        dotnet linq2db mcp <options> : run STDIO MCP server exposing read-oriented SQL query execution and optional write-capable execution as model-controlled tools
        dotnet linq2db query <options> : execute read-oriented SQL query so agents can analyze code together with live database data
        dotnet linq2db schema <options> : inspect database object metadata using linq2db schema providers
        dotnet linq2db skill : print agent instructions in Markdown format
        dotnet linq2db scaffold <options> : generate database data model classes from database schema
        dotnet linq2db template [-o output_template_file_path] : creates empty T4 template for scaffolding customization

Examples:
        dotnet linq2db query --provider SQLite --connection-string "Data Source=data.db" --sql "select * from Person"
            execute read-oriented SQL query against SQLite database and write JSON result to console

        dotnet linq2db scaffold -o c:\my_project\model -p SqlServer -c "Server=MySqlServer;Database=MyDatabase;User Id=scaffold_user;Password=secret;"
            generate data model code for S

dotnet linq2db - Linq To DB command-line utilities. Version: 6.4.0.0

Usage:
        dotnet linq2db config-init <options>

Description:
        create or update a query/MCP configuration profile; generated profiles intentionally include maxRows, output, and enableExecute for manual editing

Options:

=== Configuration : Configuration options

   --config                  : path to query configuration file; supports %NAME% and ${NAME} environment variable expansion
         type: string (optional)

   --profile                 : configuration profile name
         type: string (optional)

=== Profile : Profile settings

   --description             : non-secret profile description returned by MCP linq2db_info
         type: string (optional)

=== Connection : Connection options

   --provider                : linq2db provider name
         type: string (optional)

   -l, --provider-location   : path to external database provider assembly; dependencies must be available next to it or through normal application probing; supports %NAME% and ${NAME} environment variable expansion
         type: string (optional)

   --connection-string       : database connection string; use {0} for user and {1} for password placeholders; configure provider-specific connection timeout here
         type: string (optional)

   --connection-string-env   : environment variable with database connection string
         type: string (optional)

   --credentials             : system or external credential store target containing database user and password; supports %NAME% and ${NAME} environment variable expansion
         type: string (optional)

=== Output : Output options

   --output                  : output format to write to the initialized profile
         type: string (optional)
         default: json-table
         default (T4 mode): json-table
         supported values:
               json       : JSON output
               json-table : JSON table output
               csv        : CSV output

      Configuration profiles are shar

dotnet linq2db - Linq To DB command-line utilities. Version: 6.4.0.0

Usage:
        dotnet linq2db credentials <set|list|remove|clear> [options]

Description:
        manage encrypted linq2db credential profiles in the current user's system credential store

Options:

=== Credential : Credential profile options

   --profile   : credential profile name without the automatic linq2db/ target prefix
         type: string (optional)

   --user      : database user name stored in the credential profile
         type: string (optional)

=== Confirmation : Destructive operation confirmation

   --force     : remove all linq2db credential profiles without an interactive confirmation
         type: bool (optional)
         default: false
         default (T4 mode): false

Examples:

        dotnet linq2db credentials set --profile project-a/production-read --user ProjectReader
                securely prompts for and stores a password

        dotnet linq2db credentials list
                lists linq2db credential profile names and users

        dotnet linq2db credentials remove --profile project-a/production-read
                removes one credential profile

        dotnet linq2db credentials clear
                removes all linq2db credential profiles after confirmation

dotnet linq2db - Linq To DB command-line utilities. Version: 6.4.0.0

Usage:
        dotnet linq2db scaffold <options>

Description:
        generate database data model classes from database schema

Options:

=== General : basic options

   -i, --import                              : path to JSON file with scaffold options
         type: string (optional)
         json: not allowed

      When both command line and JSON file contains same option, value from com
      mand line will override value from file for single-value options and will
       combine values for multi-value options.
      JSON property type depends on option type: bool for boolean properties, i
      nteger number for numeric properties and string for other properties.
      If property could have multiple values, it should use array as property t
      ype.
      JSON file example:
      	{
      	  "general": {
      	    "output": "c:\my\project\datamodel",
      	    "overwrite": true,
      	    "provider": "SQLServer",
      	  },
      	  "code": {
      	    "nrt": false
      	  }
      	}

   -o, --output                              : relative or full path to folder to put generated files
         type: string (optional)
         json: general.output

      If folder doesn't exists, it will be created. When not specified, current
       folder used.

   -f, --overwrite                           : overwrite existing files
         type: bool (optional)
         json: general.overwrite
         default: false
         default (T4 mode): false

   -p, --provider                            : database provider (database)
         type: string (required)
         json: general.provider
         supported values:
               Access          : MS Access (requires OLE DB or/and ODBC provider installed)
               DB2             : IBM DB2 LUW or z/OS
               Firebird        : Firebird
               Informix        : IBM Informix
               SQLServer       : MS SQL Server (including Azure SQL Server)
               MySQL  
[truncated]
